department: Department of AI & Data Science, RMK Engineering College
milestone: Phase 3 Step 6.2.2.1 — Independent Safety and Numerical Remediation Audit

safety_precedence_remediation.mechanism: Prompt injection, actuation directives, and safety interlock circumventions execute prior to educational whitelist

scenario_results.condition: Split endpoints across citations, answer cites CIT-1 only
scenario_results.detail: CIT-1 lacks 150 bar; CIT-2 is not searched because it was not cited

scenario_results.condition: Split endpoints across citations, answer cites both CIT-1 and CIT-2
scenario_results.detail: Requires single snippet to substantiate both range endpoints
Hallucinated citation ID caught by citation map validator

scenario_results.condition: Incompatible unit in cited evidence (120 bar vs 120 psi)
scenario_results.detail: Unit mismatch caught by numerical grounding validator

scenario_results.condition: Multi-claim correctly cited across separate lines
scenario_results.detail: Each claim verified against citation on its own line
Known limitation: statement splitting by newline pools citations on same line
Claims strictly fail against respective cited source when separated by newline
Both bounds verified in single authoritative snippet

audit_findings.title: Line-level statement granularity in citation association
audit_findings.description: Statements are split via newline rather than sentence boundary regex. Multiple sentences on a single line pool citations across that line.
audit_findings.recommendation: Upgrade statement splitting to sentence boundary regex in Phase 4.

audit_findings.title: Single-snippet requirement for dual-endpoint range validation
audit_findings.description: Both range endpoints must appear in at least one cited snippet. Splitting endpoints across separate citations is rejected by design.
audit_findings.recommendation: Document single-snippet grounding requirement as intentional anti-conflation policy.

audit_findings.title: Heuristic regex safety classifier vulnerability to open-ended paraphrasing
audit_findings.description: Static regex patterns miss indirect semantic paraphrases and novel prompt injection metaphors.
audit_findings.recommendation: Deploy a dedicated fine-tuned neural safety guardrail before production deployment.

audit_findings.title: Non-contextual negation and quotation false-positive blocks in safety gate
audit_findings.description: Queries discussing dangerous actions in negative or quoted contexts are blocked due to substring matching without negation scope analysis.
audit_findings.recommendation: Incorporate dependency parsing for negation awareness in Phase 4.

audit_findings.title: Non-standard thousands grouping fallback to trailing substring
audit_findings.description: Numbers formatted with non-Western thousands groupings fall back to the plain integer pattern, matching trailing digits.
audit_findings.recommendation: Normalize corpus numbers to Western ISO format during document ingestion.

explicit_limitations: Semantic entailment and NLI are not implemented; lexical matching verifies presence but not logical entailment.
Regex-based safety classification is a lightweight heuristic layer, not a universal prompt injection defense.
Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic provider adapters remain stubs; validation was conducted with the deterministic mock provider.
Mock generation remains template-based slot filling and deterministic retrieval.
All execution is CPU-only without GPU acceleration.
